newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JANZEN, STANKOWSKI SHARE FIRST-ROUND LEAD AT HONDA CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JANZEN, STANKOWSKI SHARE FIRST-ROUND LEAD AT HONDA CLASSIC.

text.p: Lee Janzen and Paul Stankowski shared the first-round lead at the Honda Classic Thursday after shooting five-under-par 67 on the brand new TPC at Heron Bay.
Five players were a stroke behind at 68, including Payne Stewart and Britain's Colin Montgomerie.

Both Janzen and Stewart came down here last month to get a preview of the new course, designed by fellow PGA Tour player Mark McCumber. "I was excited about coming here and playing. I thought it would be a fair test, even if the wind blows," said Janzen.
The wind did blow during the first round, and scores were higher than expected on this flat course with no out of bounds and almost no water.
"There's more to this course than we first thought," said Montgomerie. "Suddenly the pins were tucked away and we were playing in tournament conditions. It was tough out there.
"I don't mind it blowing. In fact, what that does is take away the 63s and 62s, but it doesn't stop people from scoring 67s and 68s."

Both Janzen and Stankowski bogeyed the 18th hole, the course's toughest. Playing into the wind on Thursday, the players produced an average score a full half stroke above the hole's par of four. For Janzen it was the only bogey of the day, and cost him sole possession of the lead.

A seven-time winner on the PGA Tour, including the 1993 U.S. Open, Janzen has not won since August of 1995 and last led a tournament in August of 1996. After a relatively poor year in 1996, Janzen's game has improved this year, his best finish a tie for second at Torrey Pines last month.
Stankowski finished his round on the ninth hole, and finished with an eagle to tie Janzen. Stankowski holed a 90 yard bunker shot with a wedge on the par five for eagle.

"It was a weird day. I didn't hit it great, but at least I hit it solid. I like playing in wind like this, it makes me focus harder. I like the challenge of trying to hit driver out there," said Stankowski, already a winner this year, at the Hawaiian Open.
After elbow surgery on New Year's Eve, Stewart is playing just his third event of 1997.

He had four birdies and no bogeys in his round on Thursday. "I let a couple of putts get away, but it was a solid round of golf. Since this is only my third tournament, I've got the enthusiasm all the guys have at the start of the year," said Stewart.
